FINDINGS REJECTED WITH EVIDENCE (recorded here so a later blind panel can see the reasoning rather than re-raise them): (a) OpenAI T-003 Major, '`_evaluate_capabilities` appends a capability entry only after all its evaluations finish, so evaluations already performed for a capability that fails midway disappear from the Resolver Evidence, contrary to REQ-004'. REJECTED. REQ-004 binds each `capability_evaluations[]` entry to carry EXACTLY one `trigger_evaluations[]` element per affected component, and AC-018 repeats that binding as an exact-set rule. A partially-evaluated capability cannot satisfy it -- in the `evaluate-predicate-failure-after-warn` fixture the aborting capability has zero trigger evaluations against one affected component. On an abort the array is necessarily incomplete either way (later capabilities are never evaluated at all); appending the partial entry would ADD a second, per-entry cardinality violation without curing the first, whereas omitting it keeps every entry that IS present well-formed. The warn half of the same reviewer's concern -- diagnostics collected before the abort being lost -- was real and is closed, by human ruling A(1) amending AC-056 (d5701194) and commit 18d90c67 restoring the forwarding in production. (b) OpenAI T-004 Major, 'T-004 promises a staged-only steps-10-13 implementation with no live-path writes, but every Block calls `_write_evidence`'. REJECTED as stated. AC-012 requires Resolver Evidence to be written on EVERY Block except two named cases, and AC-020 repeats it for the success path; the write the reviewer calls a scope breach is mandated by the frozen requirements. tasks.md's own 'staging only ... writes nothing to a live path' sentence scopes to the TRACK-EXCLUSIVE publication set (facet-manifest.yaml / capability-summary.yaml / project-context.resolved.json), which step 14 publishes and which this task's Out of Scope section assigns to T-007. PARTIALLY ACCEPTED, and deferred rather than dismissed: the reviewer's second clause is correct that requirements.md line 333-334 says the Block-path Evidence write uses 'this same transactional mechanism' -- the journaled bundle -- while the implementation uses temp-file + fsync + os.replace. The journal is step 14, explicitly T-007's own scope, so routing this write through it inside T-004 would import another task's declared scope. Recorded in T-004's Unresolved Items for T-007 rather than silently accommodated. (c) OpenAI T-004/T-005 Majors on AC-016 byte-identity: superseded by human ruling B(1) (b572fcd6), which amended AC-016 to scope byte-identity to everything except `state` and the two enforcement-derived `context_binding` digests. The reviewer's own reasoning -- that the digests' identity across the pair is internally impossible -- is exactly the reasoning the amendment adopted.
